raw_response:
I am old now, but I still look at the land the same way. This 6 mu is what feeds the family, so I do not play with it. This year I will still plant spring maize on the maize land because it is steady and easier for me to manage than cotton. Cotton takes too much picking and too much careful watching, and with some people working outside, the family labor is not as free as before. If maize comes up well, I will give it enough base fertilizer and then one topdressing when it grows fast. Water from the well costs money, so I will not irrigate too many times, only when the soil is really dry. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area. Cotton can sell for cash, but it needs more labor, more sprays, and more time in the field. At my age I cannot spread myself too thin. I will use the same local habits as before, not chase anything fancy. I would rather spend a bit carefully and make sure I still harvest something than risk a bad year by being stingy.
